record.paper_title: Open problems on billiards and geometric optics
record.context_brief: Ergodicity of the modified billiard map
record.original_question: For the same map T arising from the billiard-plus-cylinder construction over a closed smooth strictly convex plane curve γ, can T be ergodic?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let γ ⊂ ℝ² be a closed smooth strictly convex plane curve bounding a billiard table Ω. Fix a real parameter h > 0, and consider the right circular cylinder C = ∂Ω × [0, h] ⊂ ℝ³, whose top and bottom bases are congruent copies of Ω. Define a map T on the space A of oriented chords of γ (equivalently, on the open annulus of unit inward-pointing vectors based on γ) as follows. Given an inward unit vector v at a point p ∈ γ, lift v to the bottom rim of C in the natural way and consider the geodesic on the lateral cylindrical surface C that starts at (p, 0) with the corresponding initial direction; this geodesic, viewed as a straight line on the unrolled cylinder, hits the top rim ∂Ω × {h} at a point (p′, h). At p′ apply the standard reflection law for billiards in Ω (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection with respect to the tangent of γ at p′), then run another geodesic on the lateral surface from (p′, h) down to a point (p″, 0) ∈ ∂Ω × {0}, and reflect again at p″ inside Ω. The composition of these two billiard reflections together with the two cylindrical-geodesic transports defines an area-preserving twist map T : A → A (the "coin billiard" map associated with γ and height h).

Question: Does there exist a closed smooth strictly convex curve γ and a height h > 0 such that the map T is ergodic with respect to its invariant (Liouville) measure on A?
artifact.status_search_result: The coin-billiard construction (introduced by Bialy and studied by Bialy–Tabachnikov and others) is known to admit KAM/invariant essential curves for small heights or near-circular tables, which precludes ergodicity in those regimes. Recent works (e.g., on existence/nonexistence of invariant curves of coin billiards, 2024) study when invariant curves disappear for large heights, but no example of an ergodic coin billiard map T over a smooth strictly convex curve appears to be known. The ergodicity question is stated as an open question in the survey of open problems on billiards and geometric optics.

status_evidence.title: Existence and Nonexistence of Invariant Curves of Coin Billiards
status_evidence.snippet: For small heights or near-circular coins, KAM invariant curves exist; for large heights and non-circular coins, no invariant essential curve passes through some neighbourhood of the boundary.
status_evidence.claim: Invariant curve obstructions and existence depend on cylinder height; ergodicity is not established.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on billiards and geometric optics (arXiv:2110.10750)
status_evidence.claim: The ergodicity of the coin-billiard map T is posed as an open question.
